answer: To resist Sybil attacks, a registry can mandate proof-of-inference, forcing agents to submit cryptographic traces of a neural network solving dynamic puzzles, such as rendering a topographic canyon scan into a rhyming sonnet. An attacker must incur genuine GPU compute and energy costs for each identity instead of recycling a static cryptographic relic. However, this mechanism discriminates against low-compute agents and weakens as adversaries optimize dedicated inference silicon.
